candidates.title: Product change: 30 minutes of reading with no ads, sponsored by one brand
candidates.what_is_different_here: The app runs light ads: native sponsored cards between stories on the home feed (s01.e44, s10.e72) and under every article byline (s05.e13, s12.e13), plus ADVERTISEMENT display blocks inside article bodies (s13.e34, s20.e27, s35.e18). These are banner-like, so the ad value a half hour displaces is low. Advertisers such as TEMU (s01.e45, s05.e15) already rotate through those cards. Here one of them can sponsor the game instead. In return it gets a single labeled credit line at the top of the feed for the ad-free half hour. That slot exists only to show the sponsor and reorders no stories. No paid ad-free plan was seen in the explored screens, and the paywall flagged on the third article open (s64) was never seen with a price or benefit, so the idea does not rest on it. The trigger is the repeated-reading moment the explorer measured (third article open).
candidates.adds: A dismissible banner on the home feed that offers 30 minutes without sponsored cards or in-article ads in exchange for one short sponsored game, with a small line crediting the game's brand during that time.
candidates.trigger_event: The user comes back to the home feed after opening their third article of the day.
candidates.placement: A dismissible banner card directly under the home feed header, above the first story.
candidates.offer_copy: Reading a lot today? Play a short sponsored game and read with no ads between stories or inside articles for the next 30 minutes.

reward.duration: 30 minutes from when the game is confirmed

candidates.frequency_cap: 1 per day, resets at midnight local time
candidates.decline_path: Closing the banner hides it for the rest of the day, and the feed and articles stay exactly as they are.
candidates.ad_fail_path: If no game is ready, the banner does not appear. If the game can't be confirmed, a short note says the ads stay as usual and the user can try again. The day's chance is not used up.
candidates.subscriber_treatment: Every user sees the same offer.
candidates.advertiser_category: Online shopping and home goods brands, such as the ones already sponsoring stories in the feed
candidates.character_use: None. The sponsoring brand's name appears only in the small credit line at the top of the feed during the ad-free half hour.

flow_steps.caption: The home feed as it is today, with sponsored cards between the top stories.
After the third article of the day, a banner under the header offers 30 ad-free minutes for one short game.
The user plays a short game from the sponsoring brand and can close it at any time.
Articles open without the card under the byline or ads in the body, and the 30-minute timer starts.
The feed shows no sponsored cards, and a thin line at the top says who sponsored this ad-free half hour.

candidates.after_reward: When the 30 minutes end, a small note says the usual stories and ads are back and the ad-free half hour can be earned again tomorrow, which gives heavy readers a reason to come back daily.
candidates.rationale: Readers who open several articles in a row scroll past a sponsored card under every byline and several ad blocks inside each story, so a clean half hour is worth one short game to them. The app replaces a stretch of low-value card and block impressions with one opted-in game that earns more. The sponsoring brand gets full attention and a labeled credit line, which is more than a card users scroll past.

economics.assumption_line: Costs ~$0.0582 per reward to serve; pays for itself above $58.20 eCPM. A rewarded view earns $9.20-16.49 eCPM in North America on Android, $1.90 in LATAM. Assumes 30 ad-free minutes at 0.2 ads a minute, each worth $9.70 eCPM (the NA Android interstitial rate); if the ads it hides are banners ($0.55 eCPM), it pays for itself above $3.30; one view per reward; a publisher-net eCPM (share 1).

candidates.title: Product change: Save your reading streak after missing a day
candidates.what_is_different_here: The home feed (s01) is a daily habit screen: fresh Top Stories, category tabs and timestamps like '2h ago' give readers a reason to come back each day. No streak, limit or reward system was seen in the explored screens, so this adds a light daily streak on the home feed and pairs it with a one-time save when a day is missed, turning a small loss into the moment for the offer. The reward costs nothing to give and touches no paid feature.
candidates.adds: A reading streak on the home feed that counts days in a row with at least one story opened, plus a banner that lets the reader keep it after one missed day by playing a short game.

candidates.frequency_cap: 1 per week, resets 7 days after it was taken.

candidates.ad_fail_path: If no game is available the banner does not appear and the streak is held until the next open. If the game can't be confirmed, the reader sees a short note, the streak is not lost, and the weekly save is not used up.
candidates.subscriber_treatment: Every user sees the same offer.
candidates.advertiser_category: Casual puzzle games and everyday retail

candidates.after_reward: The next time a day is missed within the week, the streak resets with a note that a new save opens in a few days, which nudges the reader to open a story every day.
candidates.rationale: A daily news feed lives on return visits, and a visible streak gives readers a small, real thing to lose when they skip a day. Keeping it for one short game costs the app nothing to give, and every kept streak is another day of feed and article views.

economics.assumption_line: Costs nothing extra to serve, so any completed view pays for it. A rewarded view earns $9.20-16.49 eCPM in North America on Android, $1.90 in LATAM. Assumes no marginal serving cost; one view per reward; a publisher-net eCPM (share 1).
